messages:
Maria: Heads-up — seeing a p95 token-latency spike for several deployments in us-west1 starting ~11:10 UTC, TTFT jumped and tokens/sec dropped. Any recent changes to batching or routing?
Aj: link? can you drop the grafana panel?
Maria: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abcd/token-metrics?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now — look at the "p95 token latency (per token)" panel and the tokens/sec heatmap.
Seb: grafana alert fired too?
GrafanaBot: alert: token_latency_p95_high (state: firing) — firing_for: 2m — labels: region=us-west1, severity=page
Taylor: I have the logs for the affected hosts (gpu-rack-12). small networking flaps reported by CNI around the same timeframe, but CPU on the proxy pods also spiked.
Maria: attaching a tiny log excerpt: 
```
2026-03-15T11:09:42Z kube-proxy[pid]: conn reset from 10.2.3.45: closing stream
2026-03-15T11:09:43Z runtime: batch_flusher: increased latency for batch_id=xyz size=8 -> 180ms
2026-03-15T11:09:44Z model-runtime: token_emit p99=402ms p95=270ms
```
Aj: sounds like two compounding issues: network jitter causing interrupted batching + a model runtime tail. For dashboards we should be careful with cardinality — current p95 query groups by model_id and deployment_id which makes Grafana slow to render.
Seb: agreed — propose recording rules to precompute per-model_family and per-gpu_type percentiles + tokens/sec aggregates. keeps panels fast and reduces Prometheus query cost.
Taylor: suggestion for recording rules and panel queries:
```
# recording rule: per-minute percentiles by model_family and region
- record: token_latency_p95:1m
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[1m])) by (le, model_family, region))

# panel query (uses recording rule)
avg_over_time(token_latency_p95:1m{region="us-west1",model_family=~"gpt-.*"}[5m])
```
Maria: Nice. Also add tokens/sec as a single series: rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m]) aggregated by deployment -> then a topk(10, ...) panel so we can spot regressors.
Aj: for alert tuning, I'd lower the sensitivity for p50/p95 until recording rules land. Current alert is p95 > 300ms for 2m which is noisy during small network blips. Maybe change to: p95 > 350ms for 5m OR p99 > 450ms for 2m.
Seb: +1. Also add a slope check on tokens/sec to detect sustained throughput degradation: when tokens/sec drops >40% vs baseline for 10m.
GrafanaBot: alert: tokens_throughput_drop (state: pending) — labels: region=us-west1
Taylor: I'll open a quick runbook: add recording rules, create histogram panel, update alert thresholds, and add a dashboard drilldown link from the model-serving overview to the new per-family view.
Maria: assigning tasks: Taylor -> recording rules PR and Grafana panels; Aj -> alert rule change and testing; Seb -> run a load replay against the affected deployments to validate TTFT under synthetic traffic.
Aj: I can flip a canary after PRs merge; will run the alert burn-in with synthetic blips.
Taylor: PR in a few hours, will tag ops for review. :thumbsup: 
Maria: thanks — follow up in #eng-sre-postmortems if this needs a formal write-up.
OpsBot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-0458 (linked to thread).
Maria: closing loop: if anyone spots repeated spikes outside of maintenance window, escalate to paging.
Seb: noted. I'll also add a low-cardinality histogram metric on the runtime side to capture per-token processing time without exploding label cardinality.
Maria: perfect. end of thread.
